answer: An admission auction on a willow board stops bulk fake identities. Each epoch 100 seats open; each applicant files one key-signed bid on the thread, and the price climbs a spiral: first 45, kth 45+7(k-1), thousandth 7,038. Auditors replay the thread; a bid whose key already holds a seat burns, and rented bids fail when one key funds many. 1,000 fake identities cost 3,541,500 against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 45 once and keeps its share.
